newsitem.title: USA: Chubb life unit likely to attract buyers.
newsitem.headline: Chubb life unit likely to attract buyers.

text.p: Chubb Corp's life insurance business, which has a book value of about $842 million, is likely to attract interest from a number of possible buyers.
Chubb, in a conference call with analysts on Thursday afternoon, said it was considering a possible sale or spinoff of its life insurance and real estate businesses.

Companies that might have an interest in the life insurance business include General Electric Co's GE Capital, American General Corp, Conseco Inc and Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, industry sources said.
GE Capital and Conseco declined comment. American General and ING were not immediately available for comment.
"It's not a company that's saddled with any ugly assets. It's basically pretty clean. There's no reason for it not to attract buyers," Salomon analyst Michael Smith said.

On the conference call, Chubb chief executive Dean O'Hare said the company was reviewing its strategic alternatives for the life insurance business because it was unwilling to commit the capital needed to make it competitive.
A replay of the conference call was later made available.
"Chubb Life is a mid-sized player in a field of giants," O'Hare said on the conference call. "In today's life insurance markets, expenses are critical.
"To maximize returns we would have to expand Chubb Life's book of business to produce the efficiencies necessary to be competitive," O'Hare said.
"Such an additional commitment from Chubb may not be in the best interests of shareholders. Therefore, we feel it necessary to again consider our options," O'Hare said.
Decisions about how to proceed could come before the end of the year, O'Hare said.
Proceeds from a sale of the businesses could be used to buy back stock, make an acquisition to gain entry into an international market or expand the company's other businesses, O'Hare said.
The company's stock jumped on the news, gaining 5-3/8, or more than 11 percent, to 50-7/8 in late trading.
The life insurance business has produced only single digit returns on equity, dragging down the performance of Chubb's main commercial and personal property-casualty business.
"Life insurance never really worked for Chubb," said Leandro Galban Jr., a managing director in investment banking at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette.
"They're so good at so many other things, but it's never been a front runner for them," he said. "It's not a bad company, it's simply a question of commitment."
A company with a greater focus on life insurance might find the business attractive, he said.
"I think it will probably attract a pretty large cast of buyers," another industry source said.
